reps.exemplar: The building of canals and the opening of Great Lakes navigation marked a turning point in American economic development. As Document 1 explains, once the Erie Canal linked the Great Lakes to the Atlantic, the line of navigable water extended nearly a thousand miles into the interior, and Western states rushed to build similar works so that goods could reach market cheaply. Document 2's map shows the dense shipping network that resulted. Before these improvements the interior was isolated wilderness with 'no market'; afterward it became a settled, commercial region tied to the national economy. That shift — from isolation to integration — is why the Transportation Revolution counts as a turning point: it bound the West to the East and accelerated national economic growth.
reps.compare_focus: Contrast the 'before' and the 'after,' then explain why the change was significant — a turning point needs both sides of the pivot.
compare_checklist: Did I describe conditions before AND after the development?
Did I explain why the shift was significant, not just that it happened?
